transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. It is nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, I'm here because... I'm pretty sure the people on the environmental modeling contract I'm working on have been tracking my revisions. They're planting errors in the datasets. I think they're trying to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, but... I know what I'm seeing in the data.

Have you experienced any periods where your mood felt significantly different—like feeling extremely low, hopeless, or unusually energetic and restless—at the same time as these concerns about your work?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't felt depressed or unusually energetic. My mood has been pretty steady. I just get frustrated, obviously, because of what I'm seeing them do to the datasets, but... no, I haven't had any major shifts in how I feel overall. Just the normal stress of dealing with the project.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?
No, I haven't heard any voices or anything like that. It's just the data... the changes they're making to the files. I don't hear things that aren't there.
How long have you been noticing these changes in the datasets?
It's been about two months now. Yeah, for the last two months I've been absolutely certain that they're tracking my revisions and deliberately planting those errors in the files.
Has this situation with the datasets affected your ability to perform your job duties or manage your daily responsibilities at home?

Yeah, it definitely has. I've, um... I've fallen far enough behind on my modeling deliverables that my firm actually went ahead and reassigned pieces of the contract. And I'm supposed to supervise a few junior analysts, but I've basically stopped being useful to them lately. 

Then at home, well, I mostly just keep to myself now. My wife has had to really push me just to get me to keep basic routines going.
Aside from the concerns about the data, have you ever seen anything, smelled anything, or felt any physical sensations that seemed unusual or that others could not perceive?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't see things, and I don't smell or feel anything out of the ordinary. It's really just the data... that's the only thing that's wrong. Everything else is completely normal.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to organize your thoughts, or have others mentioned that your speech or behavior seems disorganized or difficult to follow?

No, I haven't noticed any issues with that. My thoughts are... well, they're perfectly clear to me. And my wife or the guys at work haven't said anything about my speech being hard to follow or my behavior being disorganized. Like I said, it's really just the situation with the datasets that's the problem. Otherwise, my mind is working just fine.
Are you concerned that anyone outside of your work environment, such as neighbors, friends, or strangers, might be involved in or aware of these changes to your data?

No, I don't think it's strangers or neighbors or anything like that. It's... it's specifically the people on the environmental modeling contract. I'm pretty sure they are the ones tracking my revisions. They're planting errors in the datasets on purpose to make it look like I can't lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just normal version-control mistakes, but... I know what I'm seeing. It's the people on that contract.
Are there any other situations or people in your life, aside from the environmental modeling contract, that you feel are being manipulated or directed against you?

No, no, nothing like that. It's just the contract. My home life is fine, my neighbors are just regular people... nobody else is doing anything. It's really just the datasets at work. That's the only place this is happening.
Have you noticed that you have less interest in hobbies or activities that you used to enjoy, or do you find it harder to get motivated to do things you typically find pleasurable?

Yeah, I suppose I have. These days... well, I can just sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with my telescope still covered up. I know I used to really enjoy hiking, and mentoring the younger analysts at work, and going out to astronomy nights... but lately, I just don't feel much pull to start anything. Or even to talk to anyone, really. The motivation just isn't there.
